cues: A relative clause describes a noun, and begins with a relative pronoun.
Who for a person as subject: the girl who won the prize.
Whom for a person as object, in formal English.
Which for a thing or an animal.
That for a person or thing, but only in defining clauses.
And where, when and why for a place, a time and a reason.
text: A relative clause describes a noun, and begins with a relative pronoun. Who for a person as subject: the girl who won the prize. Whom for a person as object, in formal English. Whose for possession. Which for a thing or an animal. That for a person or thing, but only in defining clauses. And where, when and why for a place, a time and a reason.
